name: Butylene glycol

lead: Butylene glycol (1,3-butanediol) is a common ingredient in serums, toners and moisturisers. It attracts water to the skin and helps dissolve other ingredients.
It appears in many products used for skin hydration and in some scalp products, so it works behind the scenes for the look of smoother, more comfortable skin.

paras: It is not used alone; it is part of formulas applied as usual.
Contact allergy is uncommon but reported, and cross-reactivity with propylene glycol has been studied.

angle.text: Butylene glycol helps formulations deliver their other ingredients and keeps skin moist.

lead: Butanediol, also called butylene glycol, refers to four structural isomers; 1,3-butanediol is the one common in cosmetics.[1]
It serves as a solvent and humectant in skincare and hair-care formulas. Studies of topical products list it among excipients in minoxidil solutions and hair tonics.[2][3]
A 2024 article examined cross-reactivity between propylene glycol and butylene glycol in contact dermatitis.[4]

paras: Propylene glycol, a related glycol, is an established contact allergen; estimates of allergy range from 0.8% to 3.5% depending on concentration, and it was named 2018 Allergen of the Year by the American Contact Dermatitis Society.[5] A 2024 study looked at whether people reacting to propylene glycol also react to butylene glycol.[4]

No studies found testing butylene glycol alone for appearance outcomes. It appears as a formulation ingredient in trials of topical products, such as a green tea hair tonic and minoxidil formulations.[3][2]
